transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-07-21
Time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~60 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Carlos Rivera (Redwood SE), Daniel Park (Argus Head of ML), Leah Thompson (Argus Platform Eng), Ravi Menon (CTO)

Auto-summary (auto-generated, may be rough):
- Deep dive into quantization options (INT8 / FP8 / GPTQ / AWQ) and tradeoffs for Argus production workloads.
- Discussed accuracy regressions, KV cache interactions, batching/latency, and on-prem/VPC constraints (KMS/HSM).
- Agreed on pilot bench plan and next steps to run benchmarks on Argus validation set.

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick intro — I'm Maya Chen, AE at Redwood. Carlos Rivera from our SE team is here to run the technical side.
[00:08] Daniel (Argus): Hi, Daniel Park, Head of ML at Argus. Leah and Ravi from infra are also on.
[00:12] Leah (Argus): Hey all.
[00:14] Carlos (Redwood SE): Hi. Quick logistics, we'll cover quant options, perf numbers, and then get into KV cache and batching. Feel free to interrupt.
[00:22] Ravi (Argus CTO): We're primarily interested in minimizing cost while keeping less than 1% regression on our NLU scoring. Also the production context length is 8k tokens for a subset of flows.
[00:32] Carlos: Great, that's helpful. Can I confirm: current infra is a mix of GCP and on-prem GPU hosts in a colo, with a requirement that sensitive inference runs stay in your VPC?
[00:40] Leah: Correct. We want Redwood Private deployed into our VPC or dedicated nodes on-prem. KMS/HSM integration is required for keys.
[00:46] Maya: We'll cover that — Redwood Private supports customer-managed KMS and HSM on prem, and we have a checklist. I'll share it after.
[00:53] Carlos: Jumping into quantization. Broadly, options we see in the field: INT8 (symmetric/asymmetric), FP8 (EMBED/activations dynamic), GPTQ-style post-training quantization, and newer AWQ variants optimized for accuracy with 8-bit weight-only quant. Tradeoffs are accuracy vs latency/throughput and memory usage.
[01:10] Daniel: We've been running GPTQ in-house for some models but saw weird hallucination increases on our intent classifier after retraining. Concerned about accuracy regressions.
[01:18] Carlos: That's expected in some cases — GPTQ can introduce layer-wise weight noise that interacts with attention or layernorm. AWQ often gives better fidelity because it uses asymmetric quant and some per-channel calibration heuristics. But it's model and dataset dependent.
[01:30] Leah: Can you quantify — like how much worse is INT8 baseline vs AWQ on a 7B/13B model?
[01:36] Carlos: Rough numbers from our internal bench on a 13B LLM for generation: FP16 baseline throughput 100 tokens/s on an A10-like node; INT8 (weight-only) up to 1.6x throughput, FP8 can hit 1.8x in some kernels; GPTQ often gives similar throughput to INT8 but with a little overhead for dequant ops — so ~1.5-1.7x. AWQ optimized kernels can be 1.7-1.9x because we can fuse ops. Accuracy-wise, AWQ typically reduces perplexity delta vs bfloat16 relative to naive INT8 — maybe the delta halves, but on sensitive classification tasks you can still see regressions 0.3-1.5% depending on fine-grained metrics.
[02:08] Ravi: That 0.3-1.5% — for us even 0.5% is a problem on some flows. How do we validate?
[02:14] Carlos: We recommend a three-stage validation: 1) offline eval on your labeled dev set (full eval metrics), 2) a holdout prompt set that stresses edge cases (paraphrases, truncated inputs, system messages), and 3) small production shadow traffic with monitoring of scoring deltas and calibrations. We'll run step 1/2 in the pilot.
[02:31] Daniel: What about the KV cache? We do a lot of multi-turn where KV cache size matters and we can't afford re-encoding.
[02:36] Carlos: Good point. KV cache interactions are tricky. With weight-only quant (like GPTQ/AWQ), the KV cache is unaffected because it's generated at runtime in FP16/FP32 depending on runtime; the cache size itself doesn't shrink unless you quantize activations as well. So batching and latency are primarily impacted by the compute kernel. But INT8 activation quantization can reduce cache memory but risks regeneration noise. Generally we keep KV cache float and quantize weights only for safety.
[03:00] Leah: So AWQ/ GPTQ won't change our KV memory footprint?
[03:02] Carlos: Not materially for weight-only schemes. If you move to activation quantization (INT8 full quant), you would see smaller runtime activations but increased complexity and more accuracy risk.
[03:12] Daniel: Latency requirements: p95 under 350ms for short prompts (<=512 tokens) and amortized cost targets for long sessions with 8k context. How do the quant methods affect tail latency?
[03:23] Carlos: Tail latency depends on kernel fusion and batching. AWQ kernels we deploy have better fusion, which reduces per-token compute and variance, so p95 tends to drop 10-25% vs naive INT8. GPTQ may add dequant steps that spike tail latency for certain layers — particularly on small batch sizes. For low-latency SLOs we recommend AWQ or optimized INT8 kernels with continuous batching disabled for the critical route.
[03:47] Ravi: Continuous batching — we currently use a latency-driven scheduler. Does Redwood support per-route batching configs?
[03:52] Maya: Yes, Redwood Console supports per-route batching/latency profiles and can pin model variants per route. You can set max batch size, max latency, and the runtime will respect that.
[03:59] Carlos: Also note caching/frequently used prefixes — if you have repeated prompts, prefix cache reduces work drastically and plays well with quantized weights. The runtime will serve cached KV fragments in fp32 so accuracy is preserved for cached tokens.
[04:14] Leah: On-prem constraints: our security team requires audit logs and SSO integration; keys must be in our HSM. Any blockers?
[04:20] Maya: We have enterprise integrations: SAML SSO, audit logs, and support for customer-managed KMS/HSM. In Private mode, control plane can be self-hosted and we can run inference in your VPC. Need to coordinate network egress rules for metrics streaming.
[04:33] Daniel: For the benchmark, we want the model to be the same checkpoint we use in prod (we'll provide a 13B fine-tuned checkpoint). How invasive is the conversion to AWQ or GPTQ? Will we need to re-run fine-tuning?
[04:43] Carlos: Typically conversion is post-training and doesn't require retraining. For some sensitive models retraining (or a short calibration pass) helps: per-channel calibration with a few hundred calibration steps on representative data reduces regressions. We'll include calibration as part of the bench.
[04:56] Daniel: Great. Also curious about tooling — can we run the quant bench ourselves in our staging cluster using Redwood tooling or do you need to run it?
[05:03] Carlos: We provide a bench harness you can run locally or we can run it within Redwood Private deployment. For on-prem pilot, it's often best to run in your staging VPC so numbers reflect network/IO. We'll hand over the harness and a reproducible script.
[05:16] Ravi: Network/IO — how big is the model artifact after AWQ/GPTQ/INT8 conversion? We want to plan disk + memory.
[05:23] Carlos: Weight-only 8-bit converts reduce model size roughly 2x vs FP16; GPTQ/AWQ are similar because they're weight-only. FP8 can be a bit denser depending on kernel packing. Activation quant reduces runtime memory but is more complex. We'll give specific sizes for your 13B checkpoint after conversion.
[05:37] Leah: Any known regressions on common safety filters or NLU scoring from AWQ conversions?
[05:42] Carlos: We've seen edge-case regressions in some safety classifiers when logits compress in certain layers — usually fixed by small calibration or fine-tuning with a tiny LR. We'll surface examples in the bench and flag any tokens with large logit shifts.
[05:56] Daniel: About benchmarks — we'd like both throughput and end-to-end cost numbers, including tokens/sec, p50/p95 latency, GPU utilization, and estimated $/mil tokens.
[06:04] Maya: We'll produce a benchmark report with those fields. We'll include cost estimates for Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private (your on-prem metrics translated into Redwood cost equivalents).
[06:12] Carlos: Technical note: when running on A100 vs H100 vs Ampere-lite nVidia cards, kernel performance varies. AWQ tends to benefit from certain tensor core paths on H100; GPTQ performance is more consistent across older hardware. We'll ask which GPU types you have in colo so we can pick the right kernels.
[06:29] Ravi: We have a mix: mostly A100s, a couple of older V100s for legacy. Does Redwood runtime handle kernel selection?
[06:34] Carlos: Yes, runtime auto-selects kernels based on arch and model shape; we'll provide a compatibility matrix. There may be manual tuning for H100 to unlock FP8 paths.
[06:42] Leah: Can you summarize the risk/benefit quick reference?
[06:45] Carlos: Sure — INT8 (weight-only): low effort, 1.4-1.7x perf, moderate accuracy risk. GPTQ: better accuracy retention for many models, similar perf to INT8 with potential dequant overhead. AWQ: best accuracy/perf tradeoff in many of our benches, 1.6-1.9x perf and lower perplexity delta, but relies on tuned kernels. FP8: high perf potential but more brittle; good for custom HW and when you can validate thoroughly. Activation quant (full INT8): biggest model size and perf wins but highest regression risk.
[07:14] Maya: Any other blockers from Argus side?
[07:17] Leah: We'll need the bench code and a list of system requirements. Also a short security questionnaire for Private deployment.
[07:23] Maya: I'll send both — security questionnaire and bench harness by end of week.
[07:27] Daniel: For acceptance criteria, if we can get <0.5% regression on our NLU F1 and at least 1.6x cost reduction for the 8k flows, we'll be comfortable moving to pilot.
[07:38] Carlos: Sounds reasonable. We'll aim to show those numbers or clearly explain tradeoffs.
[07:42] Ravi: One more ops question — during rollouts, can Redwood revert to FP16 if a regression is detected?
[07:48] Maya: Yes, we support canary rollouts and automatic fallback to a pinned FP16 variant. Console will surface metric deltas and we can set automatic rollback thresholds.
[07:57] Carlos: Also automatic sampling: we'll capture examples where model divergence is above threshold and surface them in the dashboard for triage.
[08:03] Leah: Great.
[08:05] Maya: Quick recap / next steps: Carlos will run the bench (or provide the harness) against Argus 13B checkpoint including INT8/GPTQ/AWQ/FP8, with KV cache on/off and 8k context. Carlos to share preliminary numbers by 2027-08-04. I'll send security docs/bench harness by 2027-07-23. Leah to provide staging VPC access details by 2027-07-28.
[08:25] Daniel: That matches. Any final questions?
[08:29] Ravi: No. Thanks all.
[08:31] Maya: Thanks everyone — we'll follow up in email with links to the spreadsheet and invite for the bench kickoff.

End of transcript.
